facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the audited FY2025 statements and the September 30, 2026 interim statements give a consistent filed base, and the three releases give management's adjusted measures and outlook. The debt note lists each series at December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, so the maturity profile and the September 2026 refinancing can be traced to filed text. - Strongest contrary evidence and limits: the Q3 operating result includes a large separately stated contract-termination revenue line, and the company's Adjusted EBITDA is built to exclude it while including a transition and timing benefit. The set does not let a consumer test management's split. The release outlook (October release, page:4) is forward-looking management guidance, not filed evidence. - Source risk mechanism: evidence of a one-time CommonSpirit consideration (Q3 10-Q page:5, "CHI’s payment to us of an aggregate amount equal to $1.900 billion in annual installments over the next three years") sits beside ordinary hospital and ambulatory revenue. The risk is a consumer capitalising the consideration as recurring earnings or ignoring the receivable (page:10: "The CHI Note Receivable requires three annual payments of approximately $453 million"). The downstream consequence is distorted leverage, coverage and cash conversion unless CP-1 keeps the lines apart. - Second mechanism: the interim report states compliance but not the test levels (Q3 10-Q page:51: "with all such applicable covenants and conditions at September 30, 2026"). The test levels appear only in the annual report (10-K page:148, "effective maximum secured debt covenant of 4.25 to 1.00"; page:149, "a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio to be met if the designated excess availability under the revolving credit facility falls below $150 million"). A consumer must date them to December 31, 2025 and flag that amendments after that date are not visible. - Liquidity inputs are located: cash (Q3 10-Q page:2), revolver availability and letters of credit (page:13: "we had no cash borrowings and less than $1 million of standby letters of credit outstanding under the Credit Agreement" and "we had $105 million of standby letters of credit outstanding under the LC Facility"), and the springing maturity in the annual report (10-K page:147). CP-1 must treat the borrowing base as availability, not commitment. - What cannot proceed: legal interpretation of covenants or change-of-control terms, guarantor-level or structural-subordination analysis, ratings or market-based relative value, post-October 29, 2026 monitoring, and any check of the slide deck or supplemental disclosures. - Next evidence action: supply the 2025 Credit Agreement, the LC Facility, the Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture and the other current indentures, the 8-K filings of September 22, 2026 and February 2, 2026, the Omnibus Agreement, the supplemental financial disclosures and slide deck, and any filing or release dated October 30 to November 5, 2026.

rows.label: The seven filed documents cover audited annual and unaudited quarterly statements, the debt note, liquidity and the main transaction. They are enough to start all four requested analyses, each with stated limits.
Debt, revolver, letter-of-credit and covenant text is located in the latest annual and quarterly reports, but covenant tests are described only in the annual report.
Reported revenue and the company's adjusted earnings measure treat the early-termination consideration from the Conifer arrangement differently from ordinary revenue.
The reported net-debt ratio comes from the release with no net-debt figure or definition supplied.
September 2026 refinancing is documented in the quarterly report and release but the new indenture is not supplied.
Executed 2025 Credit Agreement, LC Facility and indentures not supplied; the exhibit list cites a Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53)
Covenant test levels printed only in the 10-K (December 31, 2025); no compliance certificate or headroom figure
Net debt used for the reported ratio is neither defined nor tabulated in any supplied source
Omnibus Agreement and the 8-K of February 2, 2026 are not supplied; only the 10-Q and release summaries
Slide presentation and supplemental financial disclosures referenced by the October release are not supplied
Events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff are Not supplied
Guarantor list, restricted-group definition and guarantor-level financial information not supplied; guarantee status of the unsecured notes is not stated in the located text
Text conversion only; no original HTML or XBRL; tables are flattened
No ratings, market prices, peer data or valuation inputs (context blanks)
2026 proxy statement and governance disclosures not supplied

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Tenet is a large, cash-generative hospital and ambulatory-surgery operator whose reported leverage has fallen across the periods supplied. On the carrying amount of long-term debt, total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.30x at FY2024, 2.88x at FY2025 and 2.65x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis; net of cash it is 2.54x, 2.25x and 2.11x. Cash-paid interest cover rises from 4.69x to 5.28x to 6.03x. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is 2,674 of cash plus 1,900 of undrawn revolver availability, 4,574 in total, with nothing drawn. Debt is predominantly fixed-rate notes, 8,300 first-lien secured and 4,362 unsecured at September 30, 2026, and no maturity exceeds 1,931 until 2030. The picture is credit-supportive on its face, but four limits keep confidence at Medium: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that includes the minority share of ambulatory earnings and, in Q3 2026, a 147 favorable transition effect; operating cash flow in 9M 2026 includes 540 received from the CommonSpirit agreements; redeemable noncontrolling interests of 2,179 and operating leases of 1,257 sit outside the debt figure; and the covenant text in the sources is dated December 31, 2025.

facts.label: Latest quarter and after
facts.text: - Refinancing, September 2026: Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13). facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: - Deleveraging comes from both sides. Total debt is nearly flat between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (13,171 to 13,243) while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from 4,566 to 5,004, so the move in leverage is earnings-driven, not repayment-driven. - Earnings quality: 9M 2026 operating income of 4,547 includes 1,472 of contract-termination revenue that management excludes from Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 of 1,355 includes a 147 favorable net impact attributed to revenue-cycle transition timing (release page:2). Excluding it, LTM Adjusted EBITDA would be 4,857 and leverage 2.73x total and 2.18x net, as a sensitivity and not a reported figure. - Minority leakage: ambulatory surgery earnings are partly owned by physicians and partners. Cash distributions to noncontrolling holders of 838 over the LTM period are real cash leaving the group before debt service. On Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions (4,166), total debt is 3.18x and net debt 2.54x. - Free cash flow: operating cash flow less capex of 3,328 for the LTM period includes the 540 CommonSpirit receipt, which was offset against a payment due to CommonSpirit that sits in financing cash flows. Excluding it, 2,788. - Capital allocation: in 9M 2026 buybacks of 1,615, purchases of noncontrolling interests of 583 and distributions to noncontrolling interests of 614 total 2,812, against operating cash flow less capex of 2,961 that itself includes the 540 receipt. Cash fell from 2,883 to 2,674 over the period. The CommonSpirit agreement offset 540 owed to CommonSpirit against the amount it owed Tenet (Q3 10-Q page:5), so the receipt and the matching redemption payment inflate both operating inflows and financing outflows. - Seasonality: Q3 2026 interest expense of 203 compares with Q3 cash interest of 99 (9M 2026 464 less H1 2026 365) because notes pay semi-annually; accrued interest payable rose from 81 to 213 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Any quarterly coverage ratio would mislead; the LTM basis is used.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Tenet is a diversified US healthcare services company with two reporting segments: Hospital Operations and Services, which at September 30, 2026 ran 51 acute care and specialty hospitals in eight states plus 135 outpatient facilities and the Conifer revenue cycle business, and Ambulatory Care, which holds interests in surgery centers and surgical hospitals through USPI. The business is revenue-durable in the sense that demand for hospital and surgical care is non-discretionary and managed care contracts reprice with commercial rate increases, but the revenue base is exposed to government payment policy and to the shift of patients between payer classes. The one transaction that matters to creditors in the period is the January 2026 set of agreements with CommonSpirit Health, which returned Conifer to full Tenet ownership, ends the revenue cycle contract with CommonSpirit by the end of 2026 and delivers a payment stream of 1.900 billion over three years, of which 540 million was settled by offset on January 27, 2026. The second is the September 2026 refinancing of 2,000 of 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes. No ownership change, sponsor or leveraged transaction is disclosed; the issuer is a listed company that repurchases its shares. The view is Medium confidence: documentary facts about segments, facilities, agreements and debt are strong, but control rights, board composition, shareholder-return policy and the full CommonSpirit and indenture documents are not in the supplied set.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: CommonSpirit and Conifer. The 10-K describes the position at December 31, 2025: Tenet owned 76.2% of Conifer Health Solutions and CommonSpirit Health held 23.8%, and "In January 2026, we completed a strategic transaction with CommonSpirit Health" that returned Conifer to full ownership effective January 1, 2026 (10-K page:6). The quarterly reports give the terms. On January 27, 2026 the parties agreed to conclude the revenue cycle contract by December 31, 2026, to a payment by CommonSpirit of an aggregate 1.900 billion in annual installments over three years of which 540 million was satisfied on January 27, 2026 by offsetting the 540 million due to CommonSpirit, and to Conifer's redemption of CommonSpirit's minority interest for 540 million effective January 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The residual claim is carried as a non-interest-bearing promissory note of 1.360 billion with three annual payments of approximately 453 million, the first two due in January 2027 and January 2028 and the last, with unpaid principal, in January 2029; carrying value at September 30, 2026 was 434 current and 828 long-term (Q3 10-Q page:10). The redemption cut redeemable noncontrolling interests by 846 and raised additional paid-in capital by 306 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:20). Revenue from contract termination of 646 in Q3 2026 and 1,472 in 9M 2026 is shown as a separate statement line, and the quarterly report says the transition will be substantially complete by October 30, 2026 rather than December 31, 2026, producing a cumulative catch-up that raised revenue from contract termination by 233 and net operating revenues by 97 (Q3 release page:2); those are management statements dated October 29, 2026, and the October 30 completion is a subsequent event to the September 30 balance sheet. Mechanics for creditors: the receivable is an asset payable by CommonSpirit over 2027 to 2029, the 540 offset inflates both operating inflows and a financing outflow in 9M 2026 (CP-1), and the lost contract removes the recurring Conifer revenue from CommonSpirit facilities after 2026. The amount of that recurring revenue and its margin are not disclosed in the supplied text, so the earnings effect of the loss cannot be sized. Full ownership also removes CommonSpirit as a minority holder of a subsidiary (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: New debt issue, September 2026. Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 in a private placement, with interest payable March 15 and September 15 from March 15, 2027, and used the net proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13; Q3 release page:2). A loss from early extinguishment of debt of 5 was recognised in Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3). The Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture is dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53) but is not supplied, so the covenant package, guarantees, call schedule and change-of-control terms of the new notes are Not supplied; the located text does not say whether the new notes are guaranteed. Management says the exchange "reduced our secured debt and refinanced a portion of our near-term maturities" (Q3 10-Q page:50, Management Language). The documentary effect is lower secured debt, 8,300 of first lien notes against 9,800 at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 debt table), a longer maturity profile and a higher-coupon replacement for the 5.125% secured notes. The effect on unsecured creditors is that unsecured notes outstanding rise from 2,862 to 4,362 at the expense of the secured tranche; ranking remains: secured notes and revolver ahead of unsecured to the extent of collateral (10-K page:146).

facts.label: Conflicts
facts.text: - One conflict is logged and not reconciled. The 10-K risk factors say the credit agreement, the letter of credit facility "and the indentures governing our outstanding notes contain" covenants that "restrict our ability to pay dividends, incur additional debt and sell assets" (10-K page:50, quoted in part below), while the debt note says that for the secured notes indentures "there are no restrictions on our ability or the ability of our subsidiaries to incur additional indebtedness, make restricted payments, pay dividends or make distributions in respect of capital stock" (10-K page:148). The two statements are not necessarily inconsistent, because the risk factor also covers the credit agreement, which the debt note says includes limits on debt, asset sales and prepayments, but they leave the issuer's capacity for shareholder distributions unresolved. Downstream effect: any view on buyback sustainability or restricted-payment capacity must be treated as unproven until the executed credit agreement and indentures are read. - Not a conflict: the 10-K says the Conifer transaction was completed in January 2026, while the quarterly reports say the agreements were entered into on January 27, 2026 with the redemption effective January 1, 2026; these describe an effective date and a signing date. The 1.900 billion headline and the 1.360 billion note receivable differ because 540 million was settled by offset. - Not a conflict: hospital count rose from 50 at December 31, 2025 to 51 at September 30, 2026, explained by the Nacogdoches South Campus opening in August 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:27).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the top 10 payers provide 66% of managed care revenue (Q3 10-Q page:34 and page:39). Mechanic: a payer-concentrated, price-driven revenue base is stable in volume but exposed to contract renegotiation and to payer-mix erosion, which the filing says began in 2026 as exchange admissions fell. Implication: leverage of 2.65x total and 2.11x net (CP-1 figures) is moderate for the earnings level, but a payer-mix shock would hit EBITDA before it hits liquidity of 4,574. Counter: the conflict above does not affect this view. 2. Cash conversion and non-recurring items. Evidence: 1,472 of contract-termination revenue, a 147 favorable Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA effect and 540 of operating cash flow from the settlement (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:49; Q3 release page:2). Mechanic: one-time CommonSpirit items raise reported profit and operating cash flow in 2026 without recurring in 2027, while the receivable pays out through January 2029. Implication: headline earnings and free cash flow overstate run-rate capacity; monitoring should use the sensitivity figures in CP-1. 3. Partner leakage and refinancing posture. Evidence: noncontrolling distributions of 614 in 9M 2026 and a series of refinancings that extend maturities (Q3 10-Q page:4, page:13). Mechanic: cash is paid to physician and other partners and to shareholders before debt reduction, while debt is rolled rather than repaid. Implication: deleveraging is earnings-driven, so any earnings shock reverses it; refinancing risk is low through 2027 and rises from 2028. Counter: the logged conflict leaves restricted-payment capacity unproven. 4. Key uncertainty. Evidence: OBBBA provisions beginning in 2027 and Medicaid disproportionate-share reductions scheduled from October 1, 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:35 and page:36). Mechanic: supplemental payments of 1.107 billion in 9M 2026 depend on state programs that federal changes can cut or delay. Implication: this is the largest unquantified policy risk and the evidence set cannot size it.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Tenet's credit profile is sound and moderately levered, but it relies on earnings that are partly non-recurring and partly owned by partners, so the view stays at Medium confidence. The strongest support is USD 4,574 million of liquidity with the USD 1,900 million revolver undrawn, net debt of 2.11x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 6.03x, and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million transition benefit in Q3 2026 and earnings that belong to noncontrolling partners, so total debt is 3.18x on a partner-adjusted basis. What decides the outcome is whether commercial pricing and volume offset exchange coverage losses and the 2027 Medicaid changes, and whether shareholder payouts stay below free cash flow. [CP-1; CP-1A]

facts.label: Assessment
facts.text: - Fundamental credit view: sound, with moderate leverage and strong liquidity, restrained by earnings-quality and policy risk. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium. Basis: leverage, cover and liquidity figures [CP-1, Chart data and Financials tables]; payer mix, policy and Conifer rows [CP-1A, Company and operating model; Transaction summary]. - Thesis: Tenet can service and refinance its debt comfortably on reported earnings, but reported earnings overstate sustainable cash available to creditors, and the improvement in leverage depends on continued margin gains rather than on debt reduction. - Confidence is below High because CP-1A judges CP-2 readiness as ready with limitations, and its gap ledger carries two High items: the CommonSpirit agreements and the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied. These limit covenant headroom, the size of the lost Conifer revenue and distribution capacity; they are stated once here and in Gaps.

- Thesis: Tenet can service and refinance its debt comfortably on reported earnings, but reported earnings overstate sustainable cash available to creditors, and the improvement in leverage depends on continued margin gains rather than on debt reduction.

- Confidence is below High because CP-1A judges CP-2 readiness as ready with limitations, and its gap ledger carries two High items: the CommonSpirit agreements and the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied. These limit covenant headroom, the size of the lost Conifer revenue and distribution capacity; they are stated once here and in Gaps.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the balance sheet and liquidity carry the credit. Tenet reports USD 13,243 million of total debt and USD 10,569 million of net debt against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million, which is 2.65x total and 2.11x net. Liquidity is USD 4,574 million, made up of USD 2,674 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver, which is 1.28x the USD 3,579 million of debt maturing through 2029. Cash interest cover is 6.03x. The September 2026 refinancing moved USD 2,000 million from 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes, so the maturity wall through 2029 is USD 3,579 million and the large maturities begin in 2030 at USD 3,493 million. [CP-1, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities tables; CP-1A, Transaction summary]

facts.text: Third, reported earnings overstate recurring cash capacity. Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million favorable transition and timing effect; without it, leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net. Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 includes USD 540 million from the CommonSpirit settlement, and the matching redemption payment sits in financing. Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated before noncontrolling interests, and distributions to partners were USD 838 million over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions gives 3.18x total and 2.54x net. These are management-attributed or analyst sensitivities, not reported covenant measures. [CP-1, Interpretation; CP-1A, Company and operating model]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, free cash flow is largely distributed. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 3,328 million for the last twelve months, or USD 2,788 million without the CommonSpirit receipt. After partner distributions of USD 838 million and buybacks of USD 1,813 million, USD 677 million remains, or USD 137 million without the receipt, before acquisitions and purchases of noncontrolling interests. Tenet therefore builds little cash buffer from operations once payouts are made. The board added USD 2,000 million of buyback authorization in June 2026 and USD 1,875 million remained at September 30, 2026. [CP-1, Calculations; CP-1A, Behaviour rows]

spans.text: # CP-0 source readiness: TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (thc)
## Request
- Issuer: TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (issuer id `thc`; registrant name as filed: Tenet Healthcare Corporation, NYSE: THC), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05 (context).

- Run `thc-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025. The requested consumers are CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned files and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?

- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This answer gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates nothing.

- Locators: `page:N` is the source chunk number in the pinned `.jsonl` text, not the printed page. Earnings-release text also carries its own printed "Page N" labels, which differ from the chunk numbers.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed documents cover audited annual and unaudited quarterly statements, the debt note, liquidity and the main transaction. They are enough to start all four requested analyses, each with stated limits. | Medium | Credit agreement, indentures, slide decks and anything after the latest earnings release are not supplied; covenant definitions cannot be checked. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt, revolver, letter-of-credit and covenant text is located in the latest annual and quarterly reports, but covenant tests are described only in the annual report. | Covenant headroom needs the executed documents, so any headroom view must rest on company wording alone. | Medium |

| Reported revenue and the company's adjusted earnings measure treat the early-termination consideration from the Conifer arrangement differently from ordinary revenue. | A reader who mixes the revenue lines or the adjusted measure overstates or understates recurring cash earnings. | High |
| The reported net-debt ratio comes from the release with no net-debt figure or definition supplied. | The ratio cannot be rebuilt from the sources, so it is attributed to management only. | High |
| September 2026 refinancing is documented in the quarterly report and release but the new indenture is not supplied. | New-note terms beyond the quarterly summary cannot be verified. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient to run CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, each with limitations. Audited FY2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim reports (the latest for the quarter ended September 30, 2026) and three issuer earnings releases are located and internally dated before the cutoff. The set cannot support work that depends on executed legal terms, guarantor-level detail, ratings, market pricing, slide decks or events after October 29, 2026. Those gaps are bounded and none blocks a consumer outright, so no consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 and unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 statements, debt note, liquidity text and non-GAAP reconciliations are located. Cash flows are year-to-date, so discrete quarters need subtraction by the consumer. No XBRL or original HTML. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, the Conifer and CommonSpirit agreements, ownership interests and the September 2026 refinancing are located. The Omnibus Agreement, the 8-K of February 2, 2026 and the new indenture are not supplied. |
| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Can synthesize from CP-1 and CP-1A plus located covenant, liquidity and debt-structure text. Executed credit documents and ratings are not supplied. |
| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | All sources are chunked text with stable locators, so claims can be traced. Layout and visual checks against the filed HTML are not possible. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report; original authority for audited consolidated statements. page:1 states "Annual report pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025".
- Audit: page:113 states "our report dated February 17, 2026, expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements"; signature page:184 "Date: February 17, 2026".

- Content located: long-term debt note and covenants at page:144 to page:149 (Note 8), guarantees at page:150 (Note 9), segment information at page:173 (Note 23) and the subsequent-event note at page:175 (Note 25).
- Perimeter: consolidated Tenet Healthcare Corporation and subsidiaries, including noncontrolling interests. Units are USD millions unless stated.

- Version relationship: the oldest of the three filing families. It controls FY2025 and December 31, 2025 facts, and it is the only supplied source that prints the covenant text, the credit agreement terms and the maturity ladder as of December 31, 2025.
#### Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

- Family and authority: filed, unaudited condensed reports. Each is separate and active; none replaces another. Period and signature evidence: the Q1 report is for the "quarterly period ended March 31, 2026" (page:1) and is dated "Date: April 30, 2026" (page:50); the Q2 report is for the "quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" (page:1) and is dated "Date: July 29, 2026" (page:57); the Q3 report is for the "quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" (page:1) and is dated "Date: October 29, 2026" (page:54).

- Q3 report (`10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl`) is the latest and controls the September 30, 2026 balance sheet (page:2), nine-month statements of operations (page:2 and page:3), nine-month cash flows (page:3 and page:4), Note 5 debt (page:12 and page:13), segment note (page:24 and page:25), liquidity (page:49 to page:51) and the market-risk maturity table (page:52).

- Q1 and Q2 reports (`10-Q_2026-03-31_thc-20260331.htm.jsonl`, `10-Q_2026-06-30_thc-20260630.htm.jsonl`) supply the earlier 2026 quarter ends, the three-month and six-month comparisons and the debt note at each date (page:12 and page:13 in each). They are needed for any discrete Q2 or Q3 cash-flow derivation, because cash flows are year-to-date in every 10-Q.

- Basis: unaudited, with interim notes condensed. Page:6 of the Q3 report states that the interim notes omit "certain notes and disclosures that substantially duplicate those in our Annual Report", so covenant detail and some policies are only in the 10-K.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1) of April 30, July 23 and October 29, 2026

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1; management-prepared, unaudited, with non-GAAP measures. They are attributed management claims, not filed-statement authority. Dates: "DALLAS — April 30, 2026" (page:1 of the first), "DALLAS — July 23, 2026" (page:1 of the second) and the October release (`EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl`) which opens "Tenet Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results; Raises 2026 Financial Outlook" (page:1).

- What they add beyond the 10-Qs: Adjusted EBITDA definition and reconciliations (page:8 to page:15 of the October release), full-year Outlook (page:4 and page:5), adjusted free cash flow, and the net-debt-to-Adjusted-EBITDA ratio quoted on page:2.
- Version relationship: statement-of-operations figures repeat the 10-Q. The 10-Q controls those facts; the release is not independent corroboration of them.
#### Context (`context`)
- Run settings only. Ratings, quotes, deal terms, guarantors, borrower, parent, sponsor, peers and research questions are blank. A blank is not zero and not evidence of absence.
### Information-availability boundary
- Latest issuer document: the October 29, 2026 release and the 10-Q signed "Date: October 29, 2026" (page:54). Nothing is dated later in the pack.
- Cover-page share count is stated as of October 23, 2026 (page:1 of the Q3 report).
- The cutoff is November 5, 2026. Events between October 29, 2026 and the cutoff are Not supplied, not absent.

- The release says a "slide presentation associated with the webcast" and a supplemental financial disclosures document were to be posted on the company website (October release, page:5). Neither is in the pack.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Tenet Healthcare Corporation, a Nevada corporation, Commission File Number 1-7293, with common stock and "6.875% Senior Notes due 2031" listed (Q3 10-Q, page:1). Statements are consolidated with subsidiaries.

- Operating segments: Hospital Operations and Services, and Ambulatory Care (USPI Holding Company, Inc. and subsidiaries), per Note 1 (Q3 10-Q, page:5). Conifer Health Solutions, LLC was owned 76.2 percent at December 31, 2025 and wholly owned at September 30, 2026 (same page).

- Debt issuer: Tenet Healthcare Corporation. Secured notes are guaranteed by "certain of our wholly owned domestic hospital company subsidiaries" (10-K, page:145). The revolver obligations are "guaranteed by certain of our domestic wholly owned subsidiaries" (10-K, page:147). The guarantor list, restricted-group definition and any guarantor-level financial information are not supplied. Unresolved: whether the unsecured notes carry subsidiary guarantees is not stated in the located debt text.

- Noncontrolling interests are material to the perimeter: redeemable noncontrolling interests of $2,179 million and noncontrolling interests of $1,971 million at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q, page:2). Consolidated debt, earnings and Adjusted EBITDA are before noncontrolling holders' shares; consumers must not treat consolidated Adjusted EBITDA as available to the issuer's creditors without that caveat.
- Currency and units: USD; the Q3 report states amounts are "expressed in millions (except per‑share amounts)" except where noted. The context currency matches the sources.
### Version relationships and conflicts
- Three quarterly reports, one annual report and three releases are distinct dated documents. None is a duplicate, draft or amendment. No unsigned or draft material is present.

- Presentation difference, not a conflict: revenue from contract termination is a separate line on the statement of operations (Q3 10-Q, page:2: "Revenue from contract termination 646 — 1,472 —"), while the release says the outlook for net operating revenues excludes it (October release, page:4: "Contract termination revenue recognized from the early conclusion of the RCM Agreements is not included in net operating revenues"). Consumers must keep the two revenue lines separate.

- Basis difference, not a conflict: the debt note total (Q3 10-Q page:12, "Total long-term debt 13,243 13,171") and the market-risk table total (page:52, "Fixed-rate long-term debt $ 27 $ 157 $ 1,931 $ 1,464 $ 3,493 $ 6,269 $ 13,341 $ 12,886") are stated on different bases; the market-risk table states that "unamortized discounts and issue costs are excluded from the table". The 10-K ladder (page:149) includes finance lease obligations. A consumer must not mix the three totals.

- Management claim versus filing: the net-debt-to-Adjusted-EBITDA ratio (October release, page:2: "was 2.11x at September 30, 2026 compared to 2.33x at June 30, 2026 and 2.25x at December 31, 2025") is a management claim. No filed statement or release table supplies a net-debt figure or definition for it. The release's one use of the term is that sentence.

- Adjusted EBITDA includes a $147 million favorable net effect in Q3 2026 that the release attributes to transition activities and a timing adjustment (October release, page:2: "resulted in a favorable net impact to Adjusted EBITDA of $147 million in the third quarter of 2026"). Management attribution; the filed 10-Q segment note (page:24) reproduces the reported Adjusted EBITDA but not that split.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, non-GAAP, cash flows | 10-K page:144 to page:149; Q3 10-Q page:2 to page:4, page:12, page:13, page:24, page:25, page:49 to page:52; October release page:8 to page:15 | Cash flows are year-to-date; net debt not supplied; LTM must be built from FY2025 and nine-month columns; contract-termination revenue and Adjusted EBITDA definitions differ from GAAP lines |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, ownership, transaction history | Q3 10-Q page:5, page:10, page:13; 10-K page:175 (Note 25); October release page:2 to page:4 | Omnibus Agreement, 8-K of February 2, 2026 and new indenture not supplied; no investor presentation |

| CP-2 | CP-1 and CP-1A outputs; covenants; liquidity; refinancing | 10-K page:147 to page:149; Q3 10-Q page:13, page:50, page:51 | Covenant definitions and compliance certificates not supplied; the quarterly report states only that the company was in compliance |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven filings have chunk locators | No original HTML or XBRL; printed page labels differ from chunk numbers |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the audited FY2025 statements and the September 30, 2026 interim statements give a consistent filed base, and the three releases give management's adjusted measures and outlook. The debt note lists each series at December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, so the maturity profile and the September 2026 refinancing can be traced to filed text.

- Strongest contrary evidence and limits: the Q3 operating result includes a large separately stated contract-termination revenue line, and the company's Adjusted EBITDA is built to exclude it while including a transition and timing benefit. The set does not let a consumer test management's split. The release outlook (October release, page:4) is forward-looking management guidance, not filed evidence.

- Source risk mechanism: evidence of a one-time CommonSpirit consideration (Q3 10-Q page:5, "CHI’s payment to us of an aggregate amount equal to $1.900 billion in annual installments over the next three years") sits beside ordinary hospital and ambulatory revenue. The risk is a consumer capitalising the consideration as recurring earnings or ignoring the receivable (page:10: "The CHI Note Receivable requires three annual payments of approximately $453 million"). The downstream consequence is distorted leverage, coverage and cash conversion unless CP-1 keeps the lines apart.

- Second mechanism: the interim report states compliance but not the test levels (Q3 10-Q page:51: "with all such applicable covenants and conditions at September 30, 2026"). The test levels appear only in the annual report (10-K page:148, "effective maximum secured debt covenant of 4.25 to 1.00"; page:149, "a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio to be met if the designated excess availability under the revolving credit facility falls below $150 million"). A consumer must date them to December 31, 2025 and flag that amendments after that date are not visible.

- Liquidity inputs are located: cash (Q3 10-Q page:2), revolver availability and letters of credit (page:13: "we had no cash borrowings and less than $1 million of standby letters of credit outstanding under the Credit Agreement" and "we had $105 million of standby letters of credit outstanding under the LC Facility"), and the springing maturity in the annual report (10-K page:147). CP-1 must treat the borrowing base as availability, not commitment.

- What cannot proceed: legal interpretation of covenants or change-of-control terms, guarantor-level or structural-subordination analysis, ratings or market-based relative value, post-October 29, 2026 monitoring, and any check of the slide deck or supplemental disclosures.

- Next evidence action: supply the 2025 Credit Agreement, the LC Facility, the Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture and the other current indentures, the 8-K filings of September 22, 2026 and February 2, 2026, the Omnibus Agreement, the supplemental financial disclosures and slide deck, and any filing or release dated October 30 to November 5, 2026.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Every number above is a located quotation from a source and is not derived.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Executed 2025 Credit Agreement, LC Facility and indentures not supplied; the exhibit list cites a Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53) | High for legal work; Medium for CP-2 | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the executed documents or the exhibits to the cited 8-K |

| Covenant test levels printed only in the 10-K (December 31, 2025); no compliance certificate or headroom figure | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply credit agreement and any amendment; treat test levels as dated December 31, 2025 |

| Net debt used for the reported ratio is neither defined nor tabulated in any supplied source | Medium | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the release supplemental disclosures or the 8-K tables; until then label the ratio as management's |
| Omnibus Agreement and the 8-K of February 2, 2026 are not supplied; only the 10-Q and release summaries | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the 8-K and exhibits |

| Slide presentation and supplemental financial disclosures referenced by the October release are not supplied | Low to Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the decks; until then no deck or chart coverage is claimed |
| Events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff are Not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 8-Ks or confirm none |

| Guarantor list, restricted-group definition and guarantor-level financial information not supplied; guarantee status of the unsecured notes is not stated in the located text | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the indentures and any condensed guarantor information |
| Text conversion only; no original HTML or XBRL; tables are flattened | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML when available |
| No ratings, market prices, peer data or valuation inputs (context blanks) | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Not required for this scope; keep Not supplied |
| 2026 proxy statement and governance disclosures not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Supply if governance detail is required |
## Next module

- CP-1: use the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q as controlling for statements; keep debt, finance leases, redeemable noncontrolling interests and the CHI Note Receivable separate; keep annual, three-month and nine-month columns separate and derive discrete quarters from the year-to-date cash flows only with both periods cited; label Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted free cash flow and net-debt ratio as management non-GAAP; keep revenue from contract termination apart from net operating revenues.
- CP-1A: carry the CommonSpirit Omnibus Agreement, the Conifer redemption and the September 2026 refinancing as the central transactions; label material after October 29, 2026 as Not supplied.
- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing executed documents, the net-debt gap and the dating of the covenant text as restrictions; do not claim covenant headroom or guarantor coverage.

### Financial base view

Tenet is a large, cash-generative hospital and ambulatory-surgery operator whose reported leverage has fallen across the periods supplied. Cash-paid interest cover rises from 4.69x to 5.28x to 6.03x. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is 2,674 of cash plus 1,900 of undrawn revolver availability, 4,574 in total, with nothing drawn. ### Latest quarter and after

- Refinancing, September 2026: Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13). A loss from early extinguishment of debt of 5 was booked in Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3). The Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture is dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53).
- Revolver: availability 1,900, no cash borrowings (Q3 10-Q page:13). No amendment to the revolver in 2026 is described in the located text.

- Conifer: the transition of certain revenue cycle services occurred in Q3 2026 and was to be substantially complete by October 30, 2026, with cumulative catch-up adjustments of 233 to revenue from contract termination and 97 to net operating revenues (release page:2); these are management statements dated October 29, 2026.
- Share count: 79,588 thousand shares outstanding at October 23, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:1). Q3 2026 repurchases were 970 thousand shares for 255 (release page:2).
- Acquisitions: 201 of cash used for acquisition-related activity in 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:23).

- Management outlook (not filed evidence): FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA 5,050 to 5,200, raised by 195 at the midpoint; interest expense 815 to 825; capital expenditures 700 to 800 (October release, page:1 for the raise and page:4 for the ranges).
- Subsequent events: the Q3 10-Q describes no event after September 30, 2026 other than the share count date. Events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff are Not supplied.
### Claims outside the debt figure
- Operating lease liabilities: 1,257 at December 31, 2025 (current 214, long-term 1,043), inside other liabilities, not debt (10-K page:143). No September 30, 2026 balance is supplied.
- Finance lease liabilities of 452 at December 31, 2025 are already inside long-term debt (10-K page:143).
- Redeemable noncontrolling interests: 2,179 at September 30, 2026, of which Ambulatory Care 2,134 and Hospital Operations 45 (Q3 10-Q page:20). Put-right terms are not supplied in the located text.
- Professional and general liability reserves: 317 current and 979 long-term; defined benefit plan obligations 238 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Pension funded status is not supplied.
- CHI Note Receivable (an asset, not a liability): 434 current plus 828 long-term at carrying value, payable in annual installments of about 453 (Q3 10-Q page:10).
- Revenue and collection guarantees to physicians: maximum potential payments 328, liability recorded 290; guarantees of investee debt about 83 (Q3 10-Q page:13).
- Share repurchase authorization remaining: 1,875 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53). The board added 2,000 of authorization in June 2026 (same page).
### Covenants and structure (dated December 31, 2025)

- Secured notes indentures limit secured debt by a secured debt ratio of 4.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:148, "the secured debt ratio (as defined in the indentures) to exceed 4.00 to"; the sentence continues on page:149). The indenture definition is not supplied, so reported headroom is Not calculable; first-lien notes of 8,300 over LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 5,004 is 1.66x on this report's own simple basis, not the indenture ratio.
- The letter of credit facility has an "effective maximum secured debt covenant of 4.25 to 1.00" (10-K page:148).

- The revolver has a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio "to be met if the designated excess availability under the revolving credit facility falls below $150 million" (10-K page:149). Availability is 1,900, so the test is not engaged on the printed figures.
- Cash dominion applies if unused availability falls below 200 for three consecutive business days (10-K page:149).
- The company states compliance with all applicable covenants at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:51).

- Springing maturity: the revolver terminates on the earlier of November 4, 2030 or 45 business days before certain 2028 and 2027 to 2030 note maturities unless extended, repaid, refinanced or an excess availability condition is met (10-K page:147). The 6.125% unsecured notes due 2028 remain outstanding at 1,250, so the clause is relevant; its exact operation needs the executed agreement.
- Change of control: senior secured notes carry a 101% purchase right (10-K page:146).
### Correction to the earlier handoff

The source-readiness handoff stated that the reported net-debt ratio could not be rebuilt because no net-debt figure or definition is supplied. That remains true of the definition, but the ratio can be reproduced: carrying long-term debt less balance-sheet cash over LTM Adjusted EBITDA gives 2.25x at December 31, 2025, 2.33x at June 30, 2026 and 2.11x at September 30, 2026, equal to the three ratios in the release. This report therefore uses those inputs and labels the ratio as reproduced, not as defined by the issuer.
### Interpretation

- Deleveraging comes from both sides. Total debt is nearly flat between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (13,171 to 13,243) while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from 4,566 to 5,004, so the move in leverage is earnings-driven, not repayment-driven.

- Earnings quality: 9M 2026 operating income of 4,547 includes 1,472 of contract-termination revenue that management excludes from Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 of 1,355 includes a 147 favorable net impact attributed to revenue-cycle transition timing (release page:2). Excluding it, LTM Adjusted EBITDA would be 4,857 and leverage 2.73x total and 2.18x net, as a sensitivity and not a reported figure.

- Minority leakage: ambulatory surgery earnings are partly owned by physicians and partners. Cash distributions to noncontrolling holders of 838 over the LTM period are real cash leaving the group before debt service. On Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions (4,166), total debt is 3.18x and net debt 2.54x.

- Free cash flow: operating cash flow less capex of 3,328 for the LTM period includes the 540 CommonSpirit receipt, which was offset against a payment due to CommonSpirit that sits in financing cash flows. Excluding it, 2,788.

- Capital allocation: in 9M 2026 buybacks of 1,615, purchases of noncontrolling interests of 583 and distributions to noncontrolling interests of 614 total 2,812, against operating cash flow less capex of 2,961 that itself includes the 540 receipt. Cash fell from 2,883 to 2,674 over the period. The CommonSpirit agreement offset 540 owed to CommonSpirit against the amount it owed Tenet (Q3 10-Q page:5), so the receipt and the matching redemption payment inflate both operating inflows and financing outflows.

- Seasonality: Q3 2026 interest expense of 203 compares with Q3 cash interest of 99 (9M 2026 464 less H1 2026 365) because notes pay semi-annually; accrued interest payable rose from 81 to 213 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Any quarterly coverage ratio would mislead; the LTM basis is used.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Tenet is a large, geographically concentrated hospital operator with a growing, high-margin surgery business. The main change is the CommonSpirit exit from Conifer and the September 2026 refinancing, with steady share buybacks. | Medium | Ownership, board and shareholder-return policy documents, the CommonSpirit agreement and the indentures are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Two segments, hospitals and ambulatory surgery, with ambulatory earnings partly owned by physician and other partners. | Consolidated earnings overstate what reaches the issuer's creditors; noncontrolling distributions are a priority cash call. | High |

| The CommonSpirit agreements end a long revenue cycle contract and bring 1.900 billion of payments over three years, plus a receivable and one-time revenue. | Cash is supportive but the revenue is non-recurring and the lost contract removes recurring client revenue. | Medium |

| Revenue depends on managed care, Medicaid supplemental payments and policy; coverage changes began to cut exchange admissions in 2026. | Payer-mix and policy risk can compress margins even with moderate leverage. | Medium |

| Documented behaviour is refinancing and buybacks; no creditor-adverse action appears in the supplied text, but legal capacity for shareholder payments is described inconsistently. | Distribution capacity cannot be sized until the executed documents are read. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

Tenet is a diversified US healthcare services company with two reporting segments: Hospital Operations and Services, which at September 30, 2026 ran 51 acute care and specialty hospitals in eight states plus 135 outpatient facilities and the Conifer revenue cycle business, and Ambulatory Care, which holds interests in surgery centers and surgical hospitals through USPI. The business is revenue-durable in the sense that demand for hospital and surgical care is non-discretionary and managed care contracts reprice with commercial rate increases, but the revenue base is exposed to government payment policy and to the shift of patients between payer classes. The one transaction that matters to creditors in the period is the January 2026 set of agreements with CommonSpirit Health, which returned Conifer to full Tenet ownership, ends the revenue cycle contract with CommonSpirit by the end of 2026 and delivers a payment stream of 1.900 billion over three years, of which 540 million was settled by offset on January 27, 2026. The second is the September 2026 refinancing of 2,000 of 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes. No ownership change, sponsor or leveraged transaction is disclosed; the issuer is a listed company that repurchases its shares. The view is Medium confidence: documentary facts about segments, facilities, agreements and debt are strong, but control rights, board composition, shareholder-return policy and the full CommonSpirit and indenture documents are not in the supplied set.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

CommonSpirit and Conifer. The 10-K describes the position at December 31, 2025: Tenet owned 76.2% of Conifer Health Solutions and CommonSpirit Health held 23.8%, and "In January 2026, we completed a strategic transaction with CommonSpirit Health" that returned Conifer to full ownership effective January 1, 2026 (10-K page:6). The quarterly reports give the terms. On January 27, 2026 the parties agreed to conclude the revenue cycle contract by December 31, 2026, to a payment by CommonSpirit of an aggregate 1.900 billion in annual installments over three years of which 540 million was satisfied on January 27, 2026 by offsetting the 540 million due to CommonSpirit, and to Conifer's redemption of CommonSpirit's minority interest for 540 million effective January 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The residual claim is carried as a non-interest-bearing promissory note of 1.360 billion with three annual payments of approximately 453 million, the first two due in January 2027 and January 2028 and the last, with unpaid principal, in January 2029; carrying value at September 30, 2026 was 434 current and 828 long-term (Q3 10-Q page:10). The redemption cut redeemable noncontrolling interests by 846 and raised additional paid-in capital by 306 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:20). Revenue from contract termination of 646 in Q3 2026 and 1,472 in 9M 2026 is shown as a separate statement line, and the quarterly report says the transition will be substantially complete by October 30, 2026 rather than December 31, 2026, producing a cumulative catch-up that raised revenue from contract termination by 233 and net operating revenues by 97 (Q3 release page:2); those are management statements dated October 29, 2026, and the October 30 completion is a subsequent event to the September 30 balance sheet. Mechanics for creditors: the receivable is an asset payable by CommonSpirit over 2027 to 2029, the 540 offset inflates both operating inflows and a financing outflow in 9M 2026 (CP-1), and the lost contract removes the recurring Conifer revenue from CommonSpirit facilities after 2026. The amount of that recurring revenue and its margin are not disclosed in the supplied text, so the earnings effect of the loss cannot be sized. Full ownership also removes CommonSpirit as a minority holder of a subsidiary (Analyst Interpretation).

New debt issue, September 2026. Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 in a private placement, with interest payable March 15 and September 15 from March 15, 2027, and used the net proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13; Q3 release page:2). A loss from early extinguishment of debt of 5 was recognised in Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3). The Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture is dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53) but is not supplied, so the covenant package, guarantees, call schedule and change-of-control terms of the new notes are Not supplied; the located text does not say whether the new notes are guaranteed. Management says the exchange "reduced our secured debt and refinanced a portion of our near-term maturities" (Q3 10-Q page:50, Management Language). The documentary effect is lower secured debt, 8,300 of first lien notes against 9,800 at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 debt table), a longer maturity profile and a higher-coupon replacement for the 5.125% secured notes. The effect on unsecured creditors is that unsecured notes outstanding rise from 2,862 to 4,362 at the expense of the secured tranche; ranking remains: secured notes and revolver ahead of unsecured to the extent of collateral (10-K page:146).

Earlier issue, November 2025. Tenet issued 1,500 of 5.500% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and 750 of 6.000% senior unsecured notes due 2033, executed a new 1,900 revolver and used proceeds with cash to redeem all 1,500 of 6.250% second lien notes due February 2027 and 750 of 6.125% senior notes due 2028 (10-K page:145 and page:146). The pattern across both issuances is liability management without a priming or non-pro-rata transaction in the supplied text.

Shareholder returns. Repurchases were 1,615 in 9M 2026 and 7.99 million shares (Q3 release page:2); the board added 2,000 of authorization in June 2026 and 1,875 remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53). Share count fell from 86,952 thousand to 79,588 thousand. No dividend on common stock appears in the cash-flow statements supplied.

### Conflicts

- One conflict is logged and not reconciled. The 10-K risk factors say the credit agreement, the letter of credit facility "and the indentures governing our outstanding notes contain" covenants that "restrict our ability to pay dividends, incur additional debt and sell assets" (10-K page:50, quoted in part below), while the debt note says that for the secured notes indentures "there are no restrictions on our ability or the ability of our subsidiaries to incur additional indebtedness, make restricted payments, pay dividends or make distributions in respect of capital stock" (10-K page:148). The two statements are not necessarily inconsistent, because the risk factor also covers the credit agreement, which the debt note says includes limits on debt, asset sales and prepayments, but they leave the issuer's capacity for shareholder distributions unresolved. Downstream effect: any view on buyback sustainability or restricted-payment capacity must be treated as unproven until the executed credit agreement and indentures are read.

- Not a conflict: the 10-K says the Conifer transaction was completed in January 2026, while the quarterly reports say the agreements were entered into on January 27, 2026 with the redemption effective January 1, 2026; these describe an effective date and a signing date. The 1.900 billion headline and the 1.360 billion note receivable differ because 540 million was settled by offset.
- Not a conflict: hospital count rose from 50 at December 31, 2025 to 51 at September 30, 2026, explained by the Nacogdoches South Campus opening in August 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:27).
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the top 10 payers provide 66% of managed care revenue (Q3 10-Q page:34 and page:39). Mechanic: a payer-concentrated, price-driven revenue base is stable in volume but exposed to contract renegotiation and to payer-mix erosion, which the filing says began in 2026 as exchange admissions fell. Implication: leverage of 2.65x total and 2.11x net (CP-1 figures) is moderate for the earnings level, but a payer-mix shock would hit EBITDA before it hits liquidity of 4,574. Counter: the conflict above does not affect this view.

2. Cash conversion and non-recurring items. Evidence: 1,472 of contract-termination revenue, a 147 favorable Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA effect and 540 of operating cash flow from the settlement (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:49; Q3 release page:2). Mechanic: one-time CommonSpirit items raise reported profit and operating cash flow in 2026 without recurring in 2027, while the receivable pays out through January 2029. Implication: headline earnings and free cash flow overstate run-rate capacity; monitoring should use the sensitivity figures in CP-1.

3. Partner leakage and refinancing posture. Evidence: noncontrolling distributions of 614 in 9M 2026 and a series of refinancings that extend maturities (Q3 10-Q page:4, page:13). Mechanic: cash is paid to physician and other partners and to shareholders before debt reduction, while debt is rolled rather than repaid. Implication: deleveraging is earnings-driven, so any earnings shock reverses it; refinancing risk is low through 2027 and rises from 2028. Counter: the logged conflict leaves restricted-payment capacity unproven.

4. Key uncertainty. Evidence: OBBBA provisions beginning in 2027 and Medicaid disproportionate-share reductions scheduled from October 1, 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:35 and page:36). Mechanic: supplemental payments of 1.107 billion in 9M 2026 depend on state programs that federal changes can cut or delay. Implication: this is the largest unquantified policy risk and the evidence set cannot size it.
### Consumer judgments
| Consumer | Readiness | Take from this handoff | Why it matters | Gap | Required action |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Segments, concentrations, payer mix, Conifer terms, refinancing, partner economics, the logged dividend-capacity conflict, behaviour rows | Business risk side of the credit view and the explanation for non-recurring earnings | Ownership, board, indentures and the CommonSpirit documents not supplied | Carry Medium confidence; treat restricted-payment capacity as unproven; use CP-1 sensitivities |

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | Every locator above plus the one logged conflict and the CP-1 labelled figures | Traceability of the Conifer and refinancing claims and of the management-language rows | Text conversion only; outlook and transition-completion statements are management claims | Trace each Management Language row to its release page and check the conflict quotes against page:50 and page:148 of the 10-K |
## Calculations

No new calculation. CP-1A states figures only as located in the sources or as labelled CP-1 figures; no figure here is derived by this module. One arithmetic cross-check of a stated claim: first lien notes of 8,300 at September 30, 2026 against 9,800 at December 31, 2025 follows from the CP-1 debt table (600 + 1,400 + 1,450 + 2,000 + 1,350 + 1,500 = 8,300 and 8,300 + 1,500 = 9,800), and unsecured notes of 4,362 against 2,862 (1,250 + 362 + 750 + 2,000 and 1,750 + 362 + 750).

## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (issuer id `thc`) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, reporting currency USD. It combines the accepted financial base and the accepted business and transaction context only; no source text is re-read and nothing is quoted. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Tenet has a sound near-term credit profile: net debt is 2.11x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA and liquidity is 4,574, but earnings quality, partner leakage and payer-mix and policy risk limit the view. | Medium | Executed credit documents, ownership documents and the CommonSpirit agreement are not supplied, so covenant headroom and distribution capacity are unproven. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage and liquidity are supportive: 2.65x total, 2.11x net, cover of 6.03x and no maturity above 1,931 before 2030. | Near-term default and refinancing risk is low on reported numbers. | Medium |
| Deleveraging came from higher earnings, not lower debt: net debt rose by 281 over nine months while Adjusted EBITDA grew. | An earnings shock would reverse the improvement quickly. | High |

| Headline earnings include non-recurring items and earnings owned by partners, giving 3.18x total debt on a partner-adjusted basis. | Cash available to creditors is lower than headline Adjusted EBITDA suggests. | Medium |

| Most free cash flow goes to buybacks and partner distributions; what remains is 677, or 137 without the CommonSpirit receipt. | Little retained cash builds a buffer, so deleveraging depends on earnings growth. | Medium |
| Payer mix, exchange coverage losses and Medicaid policy from 2027 are the largest unquantified risks. | They would hit margins before liquidity, and the evidence cannot size them. | Medium |
### Credit view

Tenet's credit profile is sound and moderately levered, but it relies on earnings that are partly non-recurring and partly owned by partners, so the view stays at Medium confidence. The strongest support is USD 4,574 million of liquidity with the USD 1,900 million revolver undrawn, net debt of 2.11x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 6.03x, and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million transition benefit in Q3 2026 and earnings that belong to noncontrolling partners, so total debt is 3.18x on a partner-adjusted basis. What decides the outcome is whether commercial pricing and volume offset exchange coverage losses and the 2027 Medicaid changes, and whether shareholder payouts stay below free cash flow. [CP-1; CP-1A]
### Assessment

- Fundamental credit view: sound, with moderate leverage and strong liquidity, restrained by earnings-quality and policy risk. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium. Basis: leverage, cover and liquidity figures [CP-1, Chart data and Financials tables]; payer mix, policy and Conifer rows [CP-1A, Company and operating model; Transaction summary].

- Thesis: Tenet can service and refinance its debt comfortably on reported earnings, but reported earnings overstate sustainable cash available to creditors, and the improvement in leverage depends on continued margin gains rather than on debt reduction.

- Confidence is below High because CP-1A judges CP-2 readiness as ready with limitations, and its gap ledger carries two High items: the CommonSpirit agreements and the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied. These limit covenant headroom, the size of the lost Conifer revenue and distribution capacity; they are stated once here and in Gaps.
### Key findings

First, the balance sheet and liquidity carry the credit. Tenet reports USD 13,243 million of total debt and USD 10,569 million of net debt against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million, which is 2.65x total and 2.11x net. Liquidity is USD 4,574 million, made up of USD 2,674 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver, which is 1.28x the USD 3,579 million of debt maturing through 2029. Cash interest cover is 6.03x. The September 2026 refinancing moved USD 2,000 million from 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes, so the maturity wall through 2029 is USD 3,579 million and the large maturities begin in 2030 at USD 3,493 million. [CP-1, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities tables; CP-1A, Transaction summary]

Second, the improvement in leverage is earnings-driven. Net debt rose from USD 10,288 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 10,569 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 281 million, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 4,566 million to USD 5,004 million. Net leverage fell from 2.25x to 2.11x only because the denominator grew. Cash fell from USD 2,883 million to USD 2,674 million over the same period, after buybacks of USD 1,615 million and partner distributions of USD 614 million in nine months 2026. [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]

Third, reported earnings overstate recurring cash capacity. Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million favorable transition and timing effect; without it, leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net. Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 includes USD 540 million from the CommonSpirit settlement, and the matching redemption payment sits in financing. Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated before noncontrolling interests, and distributions to partners were USD 838 million over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions gives 3.18x total and 2.54x net. These are management-attributed or analyst sensitivities, not reported covenant measures. [CP-1, Interpretation; CP-1A, Company and operating model]

Fourth, free cash flow is largely distributed. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 3,328 million for the last twelve months, or USD 2,788 million without the CommonSpirit receipt. After partner distributions of USD 838 million and buybacks of USD 1,813 million, USD 677 million remains, or USD 137 million without the receipt, before acquisitions and purchases of noncontrolling interests. Tenet therefore builds little cash buffer from operations once payouts are made. The board added USD 2,000 million of buyback authorization in June 2026 and USD 1,875 million remained at September 30, 2026. [CP-1, Calculations; CP-1A, Behaviour rows]

Fifth, the policy and payer-mix risk is real and unsized. Managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the ten largest payers account for 66% of that revenue. Enhanced marketplace subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025 and exchange admissions have fallen; Medicaid supplemental payments were USD 1,107 million in nine months 2026 and face changes from 2027. Tenet itself says it cannot estimate the effect. The footprint is concentrated in eight states, with most outpatient centers in Arizona and Texas. [CP-1A, Company and operating model]

Sixth, the CommonSpirit exit is cash-supportive but removes recurring revenue that cannot be sized. Tenet is to receive USD 1,900 million over three years, of which USD 540 million was settled by offset, and holds a USD 1,360 million note receivable paid in about USD 453 million installments to January 2029. The revenue cycle contract ends in 2026, and the revenue and margin it contributed are not disclosed. [CP-1A, Transaction summary]
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 4,574 million of liquidity, an undrawn USD 1,900 million asset-based revolver and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. Mechanism: cash and borrowing-base availability cover near-term maturities with room to spare. Implication: refinancing and liquidity risk are low through 2029. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturities.

Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact). 2.65x total debt and 2.11x net debt to last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, with 6.03x cash interest cover, on a base of fixed-rate notes. Mechanism: fixed coupons insulate interest cost from rate moves. Implication: debt service is comfortable on reported earnings. Basis: CP-1 leverage and cover.

Scale and diversification across two segments (Documentary Fact). Fifty-one hospitals plus a surgery network of 535 centers and 25 surgical hospitals, with both segments contributing Adjusted EBITDA. Mechanism: two earning streams with different growth rates. Implication: partial offset if one segment weakens. Basis: CP-1A company rows.

Liability management without creditor-adverse action (Analyst Interpretation). Two refinancings in ten months extended maturities and, in 2026, cut secured debt; no priming, uptier or drop-down appears in the supplied text. Mechanism: orderly access to capital markets. Implication: supportive behaviour, but legal capacity is unproven. Basis: CP-1A behaviour and timeline rows.

Margin trend (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 22.6% for the last twelve months against 21.4% for FY2025. Mechanism: pricing and cost control. Implication: improving earnings supports leverage, subject to the quality caveats. Basis: CP-1 financials.
Weaknesses.

Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation). Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million transition benefit and a one-time CommonSpirit settlement that is also in operating cash flow. Mechanism: non-recurring items inflate the run rate. Implication: underlying leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net on the stated sensitivity. Basis: CP-1 interpretation; CP-1A transaction rows.

Partner leakage (Analyst Interpretation). Noncontrolling holders received USD 838 million over the last twelve months and redeemable noncontrolling interests are USD 2,179 million outside debt. Mechanism: consolidated EBITDA is partly owned by others. Implication: partner-adjusted leverage is 3.18x total; put-right terms are not supplied. Basis: CP-1 and CP-1A partner rows.

Payout intensity (Analyst Interpretation). Buybacks and partner distributions absorb most free cash flow, and net debt rose in nine months 2026. Mechanism: cash goes to equity and partners before debt reduction. Implication: deleveraging depends on earnings growth; capacity for further payouts is unproven because the supplied documents describe restrictions inconsistently. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A conflict.

Payer and policy exposure (Documentary Fact for the facts; Management Language for the policy effect). Payer concentration, falling exchange admissions and 2027 Medicaid changes against a concentrated footprint. Mechanism: price and mix drive margin. Implication: margin compression can reduce leverage headroom before liquidity is affected. Basis: CP-1A company rows.

Claims outside debt (Documentary Fact). Operating lease liabilities of USD 1,257 million at December 31, 2025, professional and general liability reserves of USD 317 million current and USD 979 million long-term, and defined benefit obligations of USD 238 million sit outside the USD 13,243 million debt figure. Mechanism: fixed and contingent claims on cash. Implication: lease-adjusted and reserve-adjusted leverage is higher than reported. Basis: CP-1 claims outside debt.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Payer-mix and coverage erosion | Exchange admissions fell in 2026 while uninsured and charity volumes rose; managed care is the dominant payer | Margin pressure reduces EBITDA against fixed debt service and payouts | Material |

| Medicaid and federal policy from 2027 | Supplemental payments of USD 1,107 million in nine months 2026 depend on state programs the 2025 law may cap or limit | Revenue and cash conversion fall; timing sits before the 2030 maturity wall | Material |

| Earnings quality and partner leakage | Non-recurring USD 147 million and settlement items; USD 838 million to partners | Underlying leverage is higher (2.73x and 3.18x total on the two sensitivities) | Material |

| Shareholder payouts | Buybacks of USD 1,813 million over the last twelve months; capacity for distributions is described inconsistently in the filings | Weaker deleveraging; monitoring posture should track payout against free cash flow | Material |

| Revolver springing maturity | The revolver ends before certain 2028 notes mature unless extended or refinanced; USD 1,250 million of 6.125% unsecured notes due 2028 remain | Liquidity backstop could shorten if the 2028 notes are not refinanced; executed terms are not supplied | Minor |
| Covenant headroom unknown | Test definitions are in documents not supplied; the interim report states compliance only | Headroom not calculable | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs are CP-1 figures in USD millions unless stated.
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Liquidity cover of maturities through 2029 | 4,574 / 3,579 | 1.278, shown 1.28x |
| Change in net debt, December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 | 10,569 - 10,288 | 281 (increase) |
| Change in LTM Adjusted EBITDA over the same dates | 5,004 - 4,566 | 438 |
| Free cash flow after partner distributions and buybacks, LTM | 3,328 - 838 - 1,813 | 677 |
| Same, excluding the CommonSpirit receipt | 2,788 - 838 - 1,813 | 137 |
| Total debt / EBITDA, EBITDA excluding 147 (CP-1) | 13,243 / 4,857 | 2.73x |
| Total debt / EBITDA, EBITDA less partner distributions (CP-1) | 13,243 / 4,166 | 3.18x |
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| CommonSpirit agreements and the recurring revenue of the lost Conifer contract not supplied | The earnings effect of the loss after 2026 cannot be sized | Revenue durability; leverage forecast | High | Supply the Omnibus Agreement and the 8-K of February 2, 2026 |

| Indentures (including the September 2026 supplemental indenture) and the credit agreement not supplied | Covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity and guarantor coverage unproven | Distribution capacity; covenant view | High | Supply executed documents |
| Ownership, board and control information (proxy statement) not supplied | Control rights and shareholder behaviour not assessable | Governance view | Medium | Supply proxy statement |
| Put terms of redeemable noncontrolling interests (USD 2,179 million) not supplied | Possible cash calls not sized | Liquidity | Medium | Supply partnership terms |
| Net debt definition not issuer-printed; reproduced from carrying debt less cash | Definition risk (for example restricted cash, leases) | Net leverage | Medium | Supply supplemental disclosures |
| Operating lease and pension data dated December 31, 2025 | Lease-adjusted leverage dated | Leverage | Low | Update from the next annual report |
| No ratings or market data | No external cross-check of the view | Context only | Low | Not required for this scope |
| Events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff not supplied | Possible later developments invisible | All | Medium | Supply later filings |
## Next module

- CP-5: trace every figure in this module to the CP-1 tables and calculations listed above; confirm the 1.28x, USD 281 million, USD 677 million and USD 137 million results from the inputs; confirm the CP-1A rows behind the payer, policy, CommonSpirit and behaviour statements; carry the unresolved dividend-capacity conflict and the two High gaps as restrictions.
